body: You can make it a separate component and then just do `<PoweredBy />`

You should be able to use the url-loader and keep the image in the raw format inside the project:

``` sh
npm install url-loader
npm shrinkwrap
```

``` js
var src = require("url?limit=10000!./logo.png");
```
I would use `px` instead of `em` to avoid having a pixelated logo.

So we're starting the BEM naming? Great!

But if so, I don't think `block` is very explicit.
If we got the BEM way, we should not use selectors that target tags, but only classes. You should add a class of  `.as-powered-by--img` on the `img` itself.

body: shrinkwrap madness! I hope npm3 will be ou soon and then Ill make sure everyone upgrades.. in the meantime we will see weird things like that but no big deal

I would not make true the default mostly because we are targeting FIRST paying customers and that you do not want a powered by (by default) to show up when you just paid for something.

Then for our integrations/community experiences we can just use poweredBy: true. It will be even more explicit for us and communities.
